description: Open-source skills softory recommends pulling instead of rebuilding. `softory skills add <name>...` (or `--recommended`) clones the pinned commit and copies the skill into .claude/skills and .agents/skills, hidden from git like the rest of softory. Nothing here is vendored into softory, so each skill keeps its own license.

anthropics/skills.license: Apache-2.0 (per skill LICENSE.txt; the document skills are source-available, not open source)

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.why: Aesthetic direction for new UI so it doesn't look like a template. Complements softory-design, which covers flows, states, and accessibility.

skills.name: web-design-guidelines
skills.why: Automated review of built UI against Vercel's Web Interface Guidelines. Fetches the rules at run time, so it needs network access; leave it out where DESIGN.md says the project loads nothing remote.

skills.name: prototype
skills.why: Builds up to three working directions behind a picker. In softory Darwin builds them as one static HTML file under docs/design/ and recommends one (softory-design says how). Manual-only in Claude (disable-model-invocation), so the role reads its SKILL.md.

skills.name: break-ui
skills.why: Worst-case data (long, empty, huge, missing, non-Latin) behind a Demo / Worst case toggle, with a fix per break. Darwin writes the fixtures; Jade wires the dev-only toggle and attaches what broke.

skills.name: emil-design-eng
skills.why: Polish, component, and motion judgement while building. Large (27 KB), so load it on ui tasks only.

skills.name: review-animations
skills.why: A strict review of motion code: easing, duration, origin, reduced motion. Darwin uses it in design review, Jade before asking for one. Manual-only in Claude, so the role reads its SKILL.md.

skills.name: remove-animations
skills.why: Removes motion on keyboard actions, frequent screens, and decoration, and nothing else. Backs the standard's calm-by-default principle.

skills.name: webapp-testing
skills.why: Playwright-driven checks and screenshots of the running app, which become evidence for UI tasks and design reviews.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.why: A strict red-green-refactor discipline. softory-testing says what to test, and this enforces the loop.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.why: Root-cause-first debugging for BUG units. It prevents guess-and-patch fixes, which waste tokens and reviews.

skills.name: verification-before-completion
skills.why: Makes agents run the checks before claiming done, which matches softory gate's evidence rule. Small, about 3.6 KB.

skills.name: ponytail
skills.why: The smallest complete change: reuse what exists, no speculative code, while never cutting validation, error handling, security, or a test for risky logic. Its own benchmark reports 45% fewer tokens and 53% less code. Pull the skill only, not the plugin's hooks.

skills.name: ponytail-review
skills.why: A lean-code lens for peer review (delete, reuse, stdlib, yagni), each finding backed by a concrete case. softory-code-review stays the procedure.

skills.name: receiving-code-review
skills.why: How to evaluate review feedback before applying it. Optional: softory-code-review covers the author side briefly.

skills.name: differential-review
skills.why: Security review of a diff with blast-radius and test-coverage analysis. This is Toby's main review tool.

skills.name: fp-check
skills.why: Verifies suspected findings before they're reported, so Toby blocks only on real issues.

skills.name: supply-chain-risk-auditor
skills.why: Audits dependencies for advisories, abandonment, and install scripts. Backs the deps tag review (OWASP A03:2025).

skills.name: semgrep
skills.why: Runs Semgrep static analysis. Recommended once the project has Semgrep installed.

skills.name: sharp-edges
skills.why: Finds footgun APIs and insecure defaults in designs. Useful when Quinn and Toby review a new interface.

skills.name: property-based-testing
skills.why: Property tests for parsers, serializers, and money or date logic. Use it when a whole input domain matters.

skills.name: react-best-practices
skills.why: React and Next.js performance rules. Only for React projects.
